Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:11:1.hebrew: מהן דתימא - הואיל ואמר רבי דוסא יד פועל על התחתונה, טעמיה משום דתפיס בעל הבית הוא. והשתא, כי פייסוהו פועלין, מצי אמר להו וכו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:11:1.english: Lest you say - Since Rabbi Dosa said [that] the laborer has the lower hand, his reason is because the employer is the one in possession [of the money]. And now, when the laborers appeased him, he could say to them, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:12:1.hebrew: סלע נותן להם סלע - ואם העתיד להעשות יכול הוא לגמרו בשכירות סלע, נותן להם במה שעשו סלע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:12:1.english: A sela, he gives them a sela - And if what remains to be done he is able to complete for a wage of a sela, he gives them a sela for what they have done.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:12:2.hebrew: לא צריכא דזל עבידתא השתא - לכך יגמור בסלע, אבל בשעת התנאי היה חציה ראוי ליותר מסלע. והן, כשפסקו על כולה ב' סלעים, דחוקים היו ואוזילו גביה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:12:2.english: No, it is necessary [where] labor became cheaper now - Therefore, he will complete [the work] for a sela, but at the time of the agreement, half of it was worth more than a sela. And they, when they contracted for all of it [for] two selaim, were pressed [for money] and lowered [the price] for him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:13:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - הואיל ולרבי דוסא יד פועל על התחתונה, נימא להו: בציר זוזא אמריתו לי — בציר זוזא שקולו; והרי הכל עושים חציה בסלע, טלו אתם במה שעשיתם סלע חסר זוז:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:13:1.english: What might you have said - Since according to Rabbi Dosa the laborer has the lower hand [i.e., is at a disadvantage], [the employer] might say to them: "You said to me [you would work for] a zuz less — take a zuz less! And behold, everyone [else] does half of it for a sela; you take for what you did a sela minus a zuz."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:13:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - דאמרי ליה: כי אמרינן לך, אדעתא דלא קים לך לעשות בסלע וראינוך שאי אפשר להוסיף, נתרצינו אנו לסלע, דהוא פחות מכדי שכר פעולה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:13:2.english: [The Gemara] teaches us - That they say to him: When we said [this] to you, [it was] on the assumption that you were not resolved to have [the work] done for a sela, and we saw that it was impossible for you to add [more]; [so] we agreed to a sela, which is less than the [standard] wage for the labor.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:13:3.hebrew: השתא דקים לך - אי אפשינו בפחות מיכן, שהרי בסלע נתרצית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:13:3.english: Now that it is clear to you - We do not want less than this, for you agreed to a sela.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:14:2.hebrew: שאני ליה בין שכירות לקבלנות - דגבי שכירות איתא להאי טעמא דעבדי הם ולא עבדים לעבדים, אבל בקבלנות אין זה עבד אלא לעצמו. ורבי דוסא בקבלנות מיירי, כדקתני קיבלו קמה לקצור, ודרב בשכיר יום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:14:2.english: There is a difference for him between hired [work] and contracted [work] - For regarding hired [work], this reason applies: "They are My servants" [Leviticus 25:55], and not servants to servants; however, regarding contracted [work], this [worker] is not a servant [to anyone], but rather to himself. And Rabbi Dosa is speaking of contracted [work], as [the baraita] teaches: "If they contracted standing grain to reap," whereas [the ruling] of Rav is regarding a day-laborer.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:1:1.hebrew: פסידא דפועלים - גשמים שירדו, הפסד פועלים הוא, דלא יהיב להו מידי, דאמר להו: מזלייכו גרם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:1:1.english: The laborers' loss - [Regarding] the rain that fell, it is the laborers' loss, for he does not give them anything, as he says to them: Your [bad] fortune caused [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:1:2.hebrew: לא סיירא מאורתא פסידא דבעל הבית - דאמרי ליה, מי יימר דלדעתא דההוא ארעא אגרתן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:1:2.english: [If] he did not survey it the night before, [it is] the employer's loss - For they say to him, "Who says that you hired us with that land in mind?"

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:2:1.english: To draw water - To water fields.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:2:2.english: And rain came - and watered [the field], and it does not need drawing [of water].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:2:3.hebrew: אתא נהרא - גדל הנהר ועלה, ונכנס בחריצין העשויין בשדה, ומהן היא שותה ואינה צריכה לדוולא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:2:3.english: The river came - The river grew and rose, and entered the trenches made in the field, and from them it [the field] drinks and does not need drawing [of water].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:2:4.hebrew: פסידא דבעל הבית - דפועלים אינם יודעין במנהג שדהו שיהא נהר עולה להשקותו, אך הוא היה יודע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:2:4.english: [It is] the employer's loss - For the laborers do not know the pattern of his field, that a river rises to irrigate it, whereas he knew.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:3:1.english: And the river stopped - From which they irrigate [the field].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:5:1.hebrew: אכלושי דמחוזא - במחוזא, שהוא עירו של רבא, היו בני אדם הרגילים לשאת משאות תמיד, וכשיושבין בטלים, קשה להן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:5:1.english: Workers of Mechoza - In Mechoza, which was Rava's city, there were people who were accustomed to always carrying loads, and when they sit idle, it is difficult for them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:6:1.hebrew: יד פועל על העליונה - ואפילו הוא חוזר בו, דיכול לחזור בו, כדכתיב (ויקרא כה) כי עבדי הם, ולא עבדים לעבדים. ומהכא יליף לה בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כב:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:6:1.english: The laborer is at an advantage - Even if he reneges, for he is able to renege, as it is written (Leviticus 25[:42]): "For they are My servants," and not servants to servants. And from here [the Gemara] derives it in the first chapter of Kiddushin (22b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:7:1.english: [Isn't it] obvious - That when they finish, it is two sela that they take.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:7:2.english: Where the price of labor increased - Laborers became more expensive.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:7:3.hebrew: ואימרו - לשון הפרש, ונזור אחור, ומתרחק מן הדבר. ובלשון המקרא דומה לו: "כעת במרום תמריא" (איוב ל״ט:י״ח):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:7:3.english: And [the laborers] rebelled [ve'imeru] - [This is] an expression of separation, turning back, and distancing oneself from the matter. And in biblical language, similar to it [is]: "When she lifts herself [tamri] on high" (Job 39:18).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:7:5.english: What might you have said - Since the laborer has the upper hand.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:8:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דאם סלע יפה מה שעשו, נותן להם סלע, אלא מה יתן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:8:1.english: Obvious - For if what they did is worth a sela, he gives them a sela; what else should he give?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:8:2.english: No, [it is] necessary where labor was inexpensive at the outset - When he hired them, laborers were inexpensive.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:8:3.hebrew: ואגרינהו בטפי זוזא - ואלו לא רצו להשתכר כשאר פועלים, והוסיף להם זוז. כשפסק להן סלע על חציה, לא היה ראוי אלא לסלע חסר דינר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:8:3.english: And he hired them for an extra zuz - And these [workers] did not want to hire themselves out like other workers, so he added a zuz for them. When he stipulated a sela for them for half of it, it was only worth a sela minus a dinar.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:8:4.hebrew: והשתא אייקר עבידתא - וקם בטפי זוזא, ששאר פועלים יטלו עליו סלע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:8:4.english: And now labor became more expensive - and [the wage] stood at one zuz more, such that other workers would take a sela for it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:9:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - הואיל ולרבנן יד פועל על העליונה, מצי אמרי ליה כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:9:1.english: Lest you say - Since according to the Rabbis the worker has the upper hand, they could say to him, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:9:2.hebrew: לא קים לכו - לא הייתם יודעים שתהיו ראויין ליטול סלע, ואני בכך היה אפשי לשכור, וראיתי בדעתכם שלא תתרצו בפחות מסלע, ואמרתי להוסיף זוז על שכר פעולה כדי ליטול סלע להשלים רצונכם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:9:2.english: [It was] not clear to you - You did not know that you would be worthy of receiving a sela, and I wanted to hire [workers] for that [amount]; and I saw in your mind that you would not be satisfied with less than a sela, so I said [I would] add a zuz to the labor wage in order [for you] to receive a sela, to fulfill your wish.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:9:3.hebrew: השתא דקים לכו - שהכל נוטלין סלע כרצונכם, על זאת לא התניתי להוסיף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 77a:9:3.english: Now that it is clear to you - that everyone is taking a sela as you desired, for this I did not stipulate to add [anything].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:2:1.hebrew: דאגר אגורי לדוולא ואתא מטרא פסידא דפועלים - משמע הכא דהלכה כרבא, דליכא מאן דפליג. ותימה: דאמר במי שאחזו (גיטין דף עד: ושם ד"ה רבה): ההוא דאמר ליה לאריסיה: "כ"ע דלו תלתא ושקלי ריבעא, ואת דלי ארבעה ושקול תלתא". לסוף אתי מטרא. אמר רב יוסף: הא לא דלה. רבה אמר: הא לא אצטריך; ומפרש טעמא דרבה משום דמשמיא רחימי עליה, ומוכח התם דהלכה כרבה! וי"ל, דדוקא באריס שיורד לקרקע באריסות, נותן לו השליש אפילו אתי מיטרא, מספק דשמא לא אתי — כמו שאר אריסי דשקלי ריבעא, אפי' אתי מיטרא לא יצטרך לדלות תלתא; אבל הכא, פועלים שאינם אריסין, אלא נותן להם שכירות על המלאכה — אפי' התחילו במלאכה, אין להם ליטול אלא לפי מה שעשו, כיון דלא נחתי לארעא להיות בחזקת אריסין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:2:1.english: "[This one] who hires laborers to draw water and rain fell, [this is] the laborers' loss" - It is implied here that the halakhah follows Rava, as there is no one who disagrees. And [this is] astonishing! For [the Gemara] says in [chapter] Mi She'achazo (Gittin 74b, and there, s.v. Rabbah): [There was] a certain [landowner] who said to his sharecropper: "Everyone draws [water] three [times] and takes a quarter [of the crop]; you draw four [times] and take a third." Ultimately, rain fell. Rav Yosef said: "Behold, he did not draw [four times]!" Rabbah said: "Behold, it was not needed!" And [the Gemara] explains Rabbah's reason: because from Heaven they had mercy on him; and it is proven there that the halakhah follows Rabbah! And one can answer that specifically in the case of a sharecropper who enters the land under sharecropping terms, [the owner] gives him the third even if rain comes, because of the uncertainty that perhaps [rain] will not come — just like other sharecroppers who take a quarter, [where] even if rain comes, he will not need to draw three [times]. However, here, [with] laborers who are not sharecroppers, rather [the employer] gives them wages for the work — even if they began the work, they are entitled to take [payment] only according to what they have done, since they did not enter the land to have the status of sharecroppers.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:2:2.hebrew: ואתא מיטרא בלילה פסידא דפועלים - לספרים דגרסי "בליליא", צ"ל דמיירי בסיירא לארעיה, דבלא סייר לא הוי פסידא דפועלים, כדאמר רבא בההוא דלעיל. ואצטריך הך דהכא לאשמועינן דבאתי נהרא פסידא דבעה"ב, דאע"ג דסיירו לארעא; דלעיל בההיא דריפקא לא שייך לאשמועינן באתא נהרא, דאין רגילות על ידי גידול נהר דתיתמלי ארעא מיא שלא תהא ראויה לריפקא בשביל כך. ומההוא דדוולא דהכא, אפילו הוה מפליג בין סיירא ללא סיירא, לא הוה שמעינן מינה ההיא דריפקא; דה"א דגבי ריפקא, אפילו סיירא לא הוי פסידא דפועלים, דלא היה להם לידע דתיתמלי מיא כ"כ ע"י מיטרא שלא יוכלו לרפוק בה, אבל הוא מכיר קרקעו שהמטר מונעה מריפקא, ולא היה לו בבקר להוליכן שם. ועי"ל דהכא גבי דוולא אפי' לא סיירא הוי פסידא דפועלים, ולהכי לא מפליג בה בין סיירא ללא סיירא כבאידך; דהתם אי לא סיירא לא הוי פסידא דפועלים, לפי שהפועלים אין להם לידע שהמטר ימנע קרקעו מריפקא, אבל בדוולא, רוב השדות מתמלאות בהם יאורים על ידי המטר, ולא היה לו לירא יותר מפועלים, ולא פשע במה שהוליכם שם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:2:2.english: "And rain fell at night, [it is] the laborers' loss" - According to the texts that read "at night" (beleilya), one must say that [Rava] is speaking of [a case] where he surveyed his land [the night before], for without surveying [it], it would not be the laborers' loss, as Rava said in that [case] above. And this [teaching] here is needed to inform us that when the river rises, it is the employer's loss even though he surveyed the land; for above, in that [case] of hoeing, it would not be relevant to teach us [the law] when the river rises, since it is not usual for the land to fill with water through the rising of a river to the point that it becomes unfit for hoeing on account of that. And from that [case] of irrigation here, even if [Rava] had distinguished between surveying [it] and not surveying [it], we would not have learned from it that [case] of hoeing; for I might have thought that with respect to hoeing, even if he surveyed [it], it would not be the laborers' loss, since they could not have known that it would fill with so much water from the rain that they would not be able to hoe in it, whereas he knows his own land — that the rain prevents it from being hoed — and he should not have brought them there in the morning. And one can also say that here, with respect to irrigation, even if he did not survey [it], it is the laborers' loss, and therefore [Rava] does not distinguish in it between surveying [it] and not surveying [it] as in the other [case]; for there, if he did not survey [it], it is not the laborers' loss, because the laborers have no way of knowing that the rain will prevent his land from being hoed, whereas in [the case of] irrigation, in most fields [their] channels fill up from the rain, so he had no more reason to fear [this] than the laborers did, and he was not negligent in bringing them there.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:3:1.hebrew: ופסק נהרא בפלגא דיומא - הכא נקט פלגא דיומא, משום דבפלגא דיומא עביד דפסיק טפי, על ידי שדולין ממנו להשקות השדות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:3:1.english: And the river stopped midday - Here [Rava] specified "midday" because at midday it is more prone to stopping, since they draw [water] from it to irrigate the fields.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:3:2.hebrew: עביד דפסיק פסידא דבעה"ב - גבי "ואתא נהרא" דלעיל, לא מפליג בין רגיל למיתי ללא רגיל, דסתמא עביד למיתי, שלכך יש בו חריצין להוליך המים בכל השדה. ולא מפליג בין בני ההוא מתא לבני מתא אחריתי, דאפילו איתנהו בההוא מתא הוי פסידא דבעה"ב, דאין להם לידע ענין שדהו אם בא מן הנהר לתוכה; אבל אם פסק הנהר, יודעין כל בני העיר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:3:2.english: [If] it is prone to stopping, [it is] the employer's loss - Regarding [the case of] "and the river came" above, [the Gemara] does not distinguish between [whether it is] accustomed to coming or not accustomed [to coming], for ordinarily it is prone to coming, since for that reason there are trenches in it to carry the water throughout the entire field. And it does not distinguish between residents of that city and residents of another city, for even if they are [from] that city, it is the employer's loss, for they are not expected to know the condition of his field—whether [water] enters it from the river; whereas if the river stopped [flowing], all the residents of the city know [about it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:6:1.hebrew: יד פועל על העליונה - כלומר, אינה על התחתונה, כדקאמר רבי דוסא שפוחת להם מה שצריך לשכור פועלין ביוקר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 77a:6:1.english: The laborer has the upper hand - That is to say, [his hand] is not the lower one, as Rabbi Dosa says that [the employer] deducts from them what is needed to hire laborers at a higher price.
